html:
From the 1840s Ireland lost people to emigration on a scale few countries have known. Its population fell from over 8 million before the Famine to under 4.5 million by 1901.

The Great Famine of 1845 to 1852 drove more than a million abroad. Emigration then became a way of life: young people left for the United States, Britain, Canada and Australia, and sent money home. From the port of Cobh alone millions sailed.

The Irish built churches, parties and unions abroad, above all in American cities such as Boston and New York. Tens of millions of people now claim Irish descent. Irish Americans paid for nationalist movements, from the Fenians to the War of Independence. Emigration remained high until the Celtic Tiger of the 1990s. Compare Norwegian emigration.
sum: From the 1840s Ireland lost people to emigration on a scale few countries have known. Its population fell from over 8 million before the Famine to under 4.5 million by 1901.
